title: Former massage therapist takes the witness stand - NewsBreak
text:
By Don Jorgensen ,
5 hours ago
SIOUX FALLS, S.D. (KELO) — The trial for the former Sioux Falls massage therapist accused of touching some of his clients inappropriately resumed today.
The state wrapped up its case Wednesday morning.
So, the defense began calling its witnesses and the first to be called this afternoon was the defendant himself, Kurt Smit.
GFP: Don’t feed the deer, it could kill them Smit walked into court Wednesday afternoon, prepared to take the witness stand and demonstrate the procedures and techniques he uses during a full body massage.
The defense even brought in a massage table into the courtroom, along with a model wearing a tight skin body suit for demonstrations.
On top of that, she was wearing only a pair of underwear, which was what all three of his alleged victims say they were wearing when they claimed Smit touched them inappropriately on their breasts and other personal places.
But before the jury was even brought in the prosecution objected to the demonstration, claiming there’s no way the defense can replicate what happened to the alleged victims or what they physically felt.
But after citing other similar court cases, the judge agreed to allow the demonstrations in the courtroom.
Smit’s defense attorney asked Smit if he’s ever touched any of his clients for sexual gratification. He replied, “Never, I have a high standard.”
But under cross-examination, the prosecution asked Smit if he remembers one of the alleged victims testifying that he touched her breasts or vagina, he said “She’s lying, most definitely lying.”
When asked if he remembers one of the alleged victims testifying that he got within a couple inches of her private parts, he said, “I was here listening to the testimony.”
The prosecution said the alleged victim told you to stop twice, and said “That should be the end of it, right?’
Smit replied, “Not always, there needs to be some discussions.”
The defense rested after Smit testified for about two and a half hours. Closing arguments get underway tomorrow morning at 8:15.
